about.title: Personal Injury Help in Monrovia, California
about.longDescription: Monrovia sits at the base of the San Gabriel foothills, where local traffic funnels through I-210, Huntington Drive, and Foothill Boulevard to reach downtown, schools, and the shops along Myrtle Avenue. In the most recent year on record, Monrovia saw 193 injury collisions, 263 people injured, and 1 traffic death — public-record numbers that reflect how much daily driving happens through this small city. Whether the crash happened merging onto the 210, waiting at a light on Huntington, or crossing Foothill near a neighborhood intersection, the aftermath is usually the same: medical bills, missed work, and a lot of unanswered questions. We provide a free initial review to injured Monrovia residents to help you understand what happened and what legal options you may have. Our team works on contingency, meaning there's no upfront cost and no fee unless there's a recovery. If you're trying to figure out next steps after getting hurt, reaching out costs nothing and there's no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling Anything

items.title: California Gives You Two Years — But It Moves Fast
items.desc: Most injury claims in California must be filed within two years of the accident, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on compensation entirely.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Mean No Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault. An insurer telling you 'you were at fault, so no payout' isn't the full picture.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering Damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California doesn't limit how much you can recover for non-economic harm like pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life. That's a meaningful difference from states that cap these damages.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning legal fees only come out of a settlement or award. There's no hourly billing and no upfront retainer to worry about.

items.question: How much does it cost to get a free case review?
items.answer: Nothing. Our initial consultation is free, and we work on contingency, which means we only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no upfront fee to speak with us about your situation.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: Yes, we provide legal representation to injured people in personal injury cases. We review your situation directly and handle your claim through settlement or litigation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the accident. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city-owned road or vehicle, the notice period can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Monrovia?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher volumes along corridors like I-210 (Foothill Freeway), Huntington Drive, and Foothill Boulevard, with reported crashes tending to peak on Fridays between roughly 5 and 7 p.m. These are neutral traffic-volume figures, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover damages even if you share some responsibility for the crash. Your compensation would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, rather than being eliminated altogether.
